newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up on tight supply.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices retained midday levels to end higher after rains reduced supply of raw materials going into the market, traders said.
But trading remained flat with overseas consumers either on holiday or unattracted to current prices, the traders said.
"We've just been sitting here shaking legs every day," said a trader with a sigh.
At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted January RSS1 buyer at 317 cents ($1.26) a kg, one cent up from Wednesday. January SMR 20 buyer was up half cent to 306.50.
Trading houses offered the SMR CV at 364 cents, SMR L at 344, SMR 5 at 318, SMR 10 at 308, SMR 20 at 307 and drum latex at 237.

Traders said producers were basically holding to current prices because seasonal rains were hampering tapping activities at plantations and reducing the flow of latex and processed rubber into the market.
The INRO five-day moving average fell to 240.31 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Dec 11 from 240.46 on Dec 10. The daily indicator price rose to 240.28 from 240.29.
